transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-03-10, Time: 10:00 PDT, Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (AtlasFin SRE), Marcus Lee (AtlasFin Head of ML), Elena Gomez (AtlasFin Security)
---
00:00 Maya Patel: okay, uh good morning everyone thanks for joining, we'll keep this tight 45 minutes. quick roll call?
00:08 Diego Alvarez: diego here from redwood, hi all
00:10 Priya Shah: priya on the call, thanks
00:12 Marcus Lee: marcus here
00:14 Elena Gomez: elena here
00:16 Maya Patel: perfect, agenda - networking updates, performance check-in on the pilot, any security/compliance blockers, and then next steps. diego want to kick off with the network status?
00:29 Diego Alvarez: yeah, quick update. we saw the initial VPC peering request come through yesterday, priya confirmed the CIDRs but we spotted an overlap with one of your analytics VPCs so we proposed small shift to the app-subnet, should be non-impacting, priya can confirm. also we recommended using an internal NLB in front of the private control-plane endpoint and configuring target group health checks with host-header. the only outstanding is the TLS cert rotation method - atlases's infra currently uses a wildcard cert that expires in june -- we suggested bringing your own cert to the nlb or using acm with export.
00:58 Priya Shah: yeah the CIDR shift is fine, we'll coordinate with infra. on the cert, elena raised concern about ACM exportability; we can't export some of our managed certs due to compliance. would the redwood private control plane accept a cert uploaded to the NLB directly?
01:12 Diego Alvarez: yes, we support uploading your PEM to the NLB or we can accept an mTLS setup between the control plane and agents if you prefer extra mutual auth. just need the cert/key and chain for the NLB.
01:28 Elena Gomez: upload of private keys to cloud provider is a compliance red flag for us, we prefer KMS-integrated cert handling or using a customer-managed HSM. does redwood support KMS-backed TLS for the control-plane endpoint?
01:44 Maya Patel: good question. redwood private can integrate with customer KMS/HSM for encryption-at-rest and key management for model artifacts. for TLS on the NLB we typically rely on customer-managed certs on the NLB layer; HSM integration for cert operations is something our infra team can pair on - it's not fully baked but we've done a customer workflow with Hashi HSM before.
02:05 Marcus Lee: from an ML side we're less tied to cert method but want zero downtime during rotations. what's the recommended rotation procedure? can we do canary NLB swap?
02:18 Diego Alvarez: recommended is create a new target group with the new cert on a new NLB listener and then shift traffic gradually; Redwood's private control plane supports DNS-based weighted routing to help with canaries. if you run into issues we have automatic fallback to the hosted control plane for admin calls.
02:36 Priya Shah: okay that helps. quick question on routing: will requests from our app in the app-subnet to the model workers hairpin through NAT? we want to avoid cross-az egress costs.
02:48 Diego Alvarez: good call. we suggest deploy the inference workers in the same AZs and use internal IPs - the control plane talks over the VPC peering, so no internet egress. we also support VPC endpoints for the artifact registry to avoid internet.
03:03 Maya Patel: moving on to performance - diego you ran the first 10k token test last week, what's the takeaway?
03:10 Diego Alvarez: correct. 10k token run with no kv cache showed avg p50 latencies ~180ms per 1k tokens for the gpt-like model we were testing on a single a100-like node. CPU usage on the orchestrator spiked during the kv serialization step. enabling prefix / kv cache in the runtime dropped per-token compute by ~28% and cut overall cost estimates by ~22% in our model. we recommended enabling the cache for your steady-state workloads.
03:39 Marcus Lee: that aligns with our expectations - most of our requests are multi-turn and have long prefixes. can we get numbers for a 50k token run? that's our upper bound.
03:46 Diego Alvarez: we're scheduling that next, maya and i think run it with both cache and without and provide raw logs so you can validate. note that for the 50k run we need to bump the worker container memory and use the newer kernel build on your on-prem nodes - older kernels had issues with hugepages and mmap that cause out-of-memory during long sequences.
04:08 Priya Shah: oof - what's the kernel requirement? our on-prem nodes currently run 5.4 kernels for compatibility with other infra.
04:16 Diego Alvarez: we recommend 5.15+ or the backported security kernel; we've seen best behavior on 5.15 and 6.x for mmap+hugepages. there's a small containerized shim we can provide to help with hugepage allocation if upgrading is difficult, but that adds complexity.
04:34 Elena Gomez: will the shim affect security posture? we need to ensure it doesn't open new surface area.
04:39 Diego Alvarez: it's a small privileged init container only for setting hugepages, with documented ops and limited runtime. we can run it under strict PodSecurityPolicies and a dedicated service account.
04:51 Marcus Lee: on the topic of model artifacts - how are model weights stored and are they encrypted? priya wants to ensure nothing persists in plain text on ephemeral nodes.
04:59 Maya Patel: model artifacts are stored encrypted at rest in the artifact store - we integrate with customer KMS for key management. runtime loads into memory and we avoid writing model weights to disk unless checkpointing via an explicit configuration.
05:15 Priya Shah: good. next, security questionnaires - elena had a few SOC2 control clarifications last week, did you get a chance to pull the baseline docs?
05:24 Maya Patel: yes i uploaded the SOC2 summary and the redwood private deployment checklist to the shared drive, elena - you should have a link in the notes. i think the outstanding items were incident response contacts and audit log retention windows.
05:37 Elena Gomez: correct. also want to confirm that audit logs are shipped to our central SIEM - syslog/forwarding is required, and retention needs to be 7 years for certain logs. can redwood forward audit logs to a customer-managed S3 or syslog endpoint?
05:51 Diego Alvarez: yes, we support pushing audit logs to an S3 bucket with SSE-KMS, or a syslog forwarder over TLS back to your SIEM. retention policy is configurable on the control plane and we can set lifecycle rules on the S3 side to match 7 years.
06:08 Priya Shah: nice. timeline question - when can we run the 50k token benchmark and also do a certificate rotation in staging?
06:15 Maya Patel: proposed windows: bench on thursday 2026-03-12 during your low-traffic hours; cert rotation in staging 2026-03-14; production rotation to be scheduled after sign-off. does that work?
06:26 Priya Shah: Thursday bench works for us if we get the network diagram Monday.
06:29 Maya Patel: i'll send the diagram monday morning.
06:31 Marcus Lee: one more thing on model variants - can we pin a specific quantized profile to a rollout group? we want to test 8-bit quantized variant without affecting 32-bit prod.
06:41 Diego Alvarez: yes, model version pinning + quantization profile is supported in the rollout config. you can create a canary route that targets a dedicated model pool running the quantized profile. routing policies let you split traffic by percent and fallback to the 32-bit variant on errors.
06:57 Elena Gomez: about data residency - some of our EU customers require metadata to remain in EU region, are you able to pin model inference for those requests to EU-only nodes?
07:06 Maya Patel: yes, smart routing supports region pinning and we can add geo-filters at the ingress so requests with EU headers route to EU-only inference pools. storage for artifacts can also be configured in EU buckets.
07:19 Priya Shah: ok sounds good. any known issues from last week's smoke tests?
07:24 Diego Alvarez: a few transient failures when the orchestrator attempted to evict pods while cache flushes were in progress - that led to a small number of failures for long-context requests. we improved eviction ordering in the latest patch and will deploy the upgrade to the test cluster before the 50k run.
07:44 Marcus Lee: what's the rollback plan if the new orchestrator causes segfaults?
07:48 Diego Alvarez: automated rollback is supported; we use image tags and can revert to previous image in under five minutes. also the control plane will route traffic away from failing nodes automatically.
07:58 Elena Gomez: asked previously about network access logs - will those include full request headers? we need to ensure PII doesn't leak to logs.
08:06 Diego Alvarez: by default network logs include source/destination and timing; request headers are redacted unless you explicitly opt in. we can offer a redaction policy and tokenization before logs leave your VPC.
08:21 Priya Shah: that's important, please include redaction config in the doc.
08:25 Maya Patel: will do.
08:28 Diego Alvarez: quick note on metrics - you mentioned wanting request-level latency histograms. we'll enable per-route tracing for the pilot and drop a prometheus endpoint behind the VPC.
08:38 Marcus Lee: good, that will help.
08:40 Maya Patel: ok, let's recap action items and owners. diego?
08:45 Diego Alvarez: i'll run the 50k-token test with kv/prefix cache enabled and without, push logs + CSV to the shared folder (due 2026-03-17). i'll also push the orchestrator patch to the test cluster before the run.
08:59 Maya Patel: i'll send the updated network diagram and exact CIDR ranges monday 2026-03-12 morning, and the SOC2/IR contacts spreadsheet. i'll also include the redaction policy template for logs.
09:13 Priya Shah: i'll confirm the change window for the NLB cert rotation (due 2026-03-15) and share infra ops contact.
09:21 Elena Gomez: i'll compile any remaining SOC2 gaps and questions and post them (due 2026-03-14).
09:29 Marcus Lee: schedule the post-bench review the week of 2026-03-18.
09:34 Maya Patel: perfect. final notes - we'll do the 50k run in staging thursday as discussed, and if green we'll propose a canary in prod the following week. any last questions?
09:45 Priya Shah: none from me, thanks
09:46 Elena Gomez: thanks
09:47 Diego Alvarez: thanks everyone
09:48 Maya Patel: thanks all, i'll follow up with notes and docs. bye.
